nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: How did Schmidt et al. (2004a) contribute to the investigation of environmental impacts?
nodes.answer: Schmidt et al. (2004a) implemented the influence of the improvement of manufacturing processes and the consequent impact at the end-of-life scenarios.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Energy-efficient production|Life cycle analysis of products_qna_001
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: Why is product lifecycle evaluation recommended in order to identify impacts along the whole value chain?
nodes.answer: Product lifecycle evaluation is recommended to identify impacts along the whole value chain in order to have a comprehensive understanding of the environmental implications of a product throughout its life cycle.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Energy-efficient production|Life cycle analysis of products_qna_003
nodes.label: Management
nodes.question: What is the significance of a life cycle assessment (LCA)-based approach in guiding the Swedish apparel sector towards sustainability?
nodes.answer: The LCA-based approach provides a comprehensive understanding of the environmental impact of the Swedish apparel sector, helping industry stakeholders make informed decisions to move towards sustainable practices.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Energy-efficient production|Life cycle analysis of products_qna_004
nodes.label: Management
nodes.question: How can life cycle assessment help in identifying environmental impact reduction opportunities in apparel products?
nodes.answer: Life cycle assessment can help in identifying environmental impact reduction opportunities by analysing the environmental impacts of a product throughout its entire life cycle, from raw material extraction to disposal, and highlighting areas where improvements can be made.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Energy-efficient production|Life cycle analysis of products_qna_005
nodes.label: Science and Tech
nodes.question: How were environmental impacts from factory production and product transportation assessed in the sustainability analysis?
nodes.answer: Environmental impacts from factory production and product transportation were assessed by calculating the global warming potential in carbon dioxide equivalents (CO2e). This involved considering emissions from textiles manufacturing, transportation to cut and sew apparel factories, and distribution centres, including container ship emissions which were found to be slightly above 1% of total emissions. Container ship worker information was not included due to lack of data.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Energy-efficient production|Life cycle analysis of products_qna_006
nodes.label: Strategy
nodes.question: What is the purpose of Waste Flow Mapping (WFM) and Inventory Analysis for Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) in the fashion supply chain?
nodes.answer: The purpose of Waste Flow Mapping (WFM) and Inventory Analysis for Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) in the fashion supply chain is to identify critical stages where waste is generated, quantify environmental impacts, and improve resource utilization and emission assessments.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Energy-efficient production|Life cycle analysis of products_qna_007
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: How can the findings in the Industrial Textile review on life cycle assessment of cotton textiles benefit the textile industry?
nodes.answer: The findings in the Industrial Textile review can help the textile industry improve sustainability practices by understanding the life cycle impacts of cotton textiles.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Energy-efficient production|Life cycle analysis of products_qna_008
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: How do life cycle based categorizations of policy differ from traditional categorizations?
nodes.answer: Life cycle based categorizations focus on different stages of a product's life cycle, while traditional categorizations are broader and do not specifically reference life cycle stages.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Energy-efficient production|Life cycle analysis of products_qna_009
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: How does the study plan to explore the implications of the proposed policy?
nodes.answer: The study plans to explore the implications through input-output (IO) analysis, which will estimate the climate and socio-economic impacts across supply chains and countries by evaluating various future scenarios regarding the policy's implementation.
